solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Poorly dressed seafood possibly stuffed with steak

indicators.note: the seafood is filled with the steak, so one word is packed inside the other

parts.note: fish is one kind of seafood, hence 'possibly'
rump is a cut of steak

explanation.surface: A restaurant review of a badly presented surf-and-turf dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poorly dressed' looks like a comment on the dish's dressing, but it is the definition of a person.
explanation.definitionFit: Frumpish describes someone in dowdy, unfashionable clothes, which is a way of being badly turned out.

clue.text: Search for gold and silver hidden by 26 in table

indicators.note: the precious metals are hidden inside the other piece, which surrounds them

parts.note: iron has atomic number 26 in the periodic table, and Fe is its symbol
or is gold in heraldry
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A hunt for precious metals concealed by an answer elsewhere in the grid.
explanation.walkthrough: '26' looks like a reference to 26 across, but it is the atomic number of iron in the periodic table.
explanation.definitionFit: To forage is to rummage or hunt about, as animals do for food.

clue.text: Cue in hand changed for free

indicators.note: changed means the letters of these three words are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A snooker player swapping the cue in their hand for nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Unchained means released from chains, so liberated or at liberty.

clue.text: Poet's continual readings maybe an impossible set-up

parts.note: perpetual means continual, never ending
Andrew Motion is an English poet, a former Poet Laureate

explanation.surface: A poet's endless readings that cannot really work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'readings maybe' describes the whole: endless readings by the poet Motion would be his perpetual performance.
explanation.definitionFit: A perpetual motion machine, running forever with no energy input, breaks the laws of physics.

clue.text: Continue moving as units

indicators.note: moving means these letters are shifted about into a new order

explanation.surface: An instruction to troops to keep going in formation.
explanation.definitionFit: To sustain is to keep something going, to prolong or maintain it.

clue.text: Good westbound road which hasn't united city

indicators.note: the reversed road lacks the letter for united, so it is taken out
in an across clue, heading west means reading right to left, so the road is turned round

parts.note: an avenue is a road
U is the abbreviation for united, as in football club names

explanation.surface: A traffic report about a westbound route that never reached a unified city.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'westbound' means read right to left, so the road is reversed before 'which hasn't united' removes its U.
explanation.definitionFit: Geneva is a Swiss city on Lake Geneva, home of many international bodies.

clue.text: Plant in flat trendy doctor grew across border

indicators.note: the word for grew goes across the border, placed after it

parts.note: even means flat or level
in means fashionable
GP is a general practitioner, a family doctor
a rim is a border or edge
rose means grew or increased

explanation.surface: A plant in a flat, a fashionable medic, something that spread across a frontier.
explanation.definitionFit: The evening primrose is a flowering plant whose yellow blooms open at dusk.

clue.text: Finale of The Who in Paris requires power supply

indicators.note: the finale of a word is its last letter

parts.note: qui is French for who

explanation.surface: The Who's final show in Paris needing power on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Who' looks like the band, but the words split: 'Finale of The' gives E, 'Who in Paris' gives QUI.
explanation.definitionFit: To equip is to provide with what is needed, a synonym of supply as a verb.

clue.text: Plate One developed to see animal

indicators.note: developed means the letters are worked into a new form, as film is

explanation.surface: A photographic plate developed to show a wildlife shot.
explanation.definitionFit: The antelope is a hoofed African or Asian mammal, a particular creature.

clue.text: Badger turned on the German waterfowl

indicators.note: turned means the word is turned round and read backwards

parts.note: to badger is to nag
der is German for the

explanation.surface: A badger rounding on a German bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' gives GAN from NAG. 'Badger' looks like the animal but is a verb, to pester.
explanation.definitionFit: A gander is a male goose, a kind of water bird.

clue.text: Appear at intervals with contingent of theatre curators

indicators.note: contingent of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Museum or theatre staff who turn up only now and then in a group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contingent' looks like a group of people, but here it marks a small part of the following words.
explanation.definitionFit: To recur is to happen again repeatedly, so something that recurs shows up periodically.

clue.text: Launched outfit outside of shop, one with diamonds?

indicators.note: the outside of a word is its first and last letters, here of shop

parts.note: an ace is the one in a pack of cards
diamonds is one of the four suits in cards

explanation.surface: A shop window display of a card player's outfit with a diamond pattern.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Launched' is part of the definition: the outfit is worn by someone launched into space.
explanation.definitionFit: An astronaut wears a pressurised garment when blasted off into orbit, so it is clothing for those launched.

clue.text: Short prayer before 8 in place of pilgrimage

indicators.note: short means cut off at the end, so the prayer loses its last letter

parts.note: grace is a short prayer said before a meal
the answer to 8 down is ANTELOPE, and an eland is an antelope

explanation.surface: A brief prayer said before a visit to a shrine.
explanation.walkthrough: '8' refers to the answer of 8 down, of which ELAND is an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Graceland, Elvis Presley's Memphis home, draws fans who travel there as if on a sacred journey.

clue.text: Little rascal followed by the Spanish force

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous child
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: A naughty child followed by a Spanish heavy who uses force.
explanation.definitionFit: To impel someone is to drive or compel them, a synonym of force as a verb.

clue.text: What stags do over in pub, one after another

indicators.note: the turned-round word sits in the pub

parts.note: an inn is a pub

indicators.note: over says the word is turned over, read backwards

parts.note: stags rut in the mating season

explanation.surface: A stag night with the party drinking in a pub, one round after another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What stags do' suggests a stag party, but it is the deer's rut; 'over' reverses RUT to TUR, put in INN.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing things in turn means taking them successively, each following the previous one.

clue.text: Rural parish initially welcomes reformed rogue for Mass again

indicators.note: the two initial letters take in the other piece between them
initially takes the first letters of the two words before it
reformed means the letters of rogue are remade in a new order

explanation.surface: A country parish welcoming back a reformed villain for Mass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mass' looks like a church service but is a verb, to gather; 'reformed' rearranges the rogue's letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To regroup is to gather together once more, as troops do after a setback.

clue.text: Strict sort of bobby regularly eschewed help

indicators.note: every other letter of bobby is shunned, leaving the alternate ones in between

parts.note: a servant is a domestic help

explanation.surface: A strict police officer refusing help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly eschewed' drops B, B, Y from 'bobby', leaving OB. An Observant is a friar of the stricter Franciscan branch.
explanation.definitionFit: The Observants were Franciscans who kept their rule strictly, so a member is a rigorous religious type.

clue.text: Understanding politician accepted in principle

indicators.note: the politician and the accepted letter go in the principle

parts.note: an ethic is a moral principle
MP is a Member of Parliament
A is an abbreviation for accepted, as on a bill of exchange

explanation.surface: A sympathetic politician accepted in principle.
explanation.definitionFit: Being empathic means sharing others' feelings, so it is a sympathetic, understanding quality.

clue.text: Reference point essential to musicians?

parts.note: the note in the middle of the keyboard is the pianist's reference point, and the letter at the middle of the word musicians is C

explanation.surface: A note on the basics every player must know.
explanation.walkthrough: The heart of 'musicians' is its letter C, so the 'essential' bit of the word is literally the middle C.
explanation.definitionFit: Middle C is the note near the centre of the piano that beginners learn first and use to find others.

clue.text: Contractors? They may require delivery at farm

definitions.meaning: leg muscles, and muscles contract, so they are things that contract

definitions.text: They may require delivery at farm
definitions.meaning: young cattle, delivered at birth on a farm

explanation.surface: Builders who need a farm delivery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contractors' suggests builders; the question mark signals the muscle sense. 'delivery' is birth, not a parcel.
explanation.definitionFit: Calf muscles tighten when you walk, and newborn cattle are delivered by farmers during calving.

clue.text: Leaving retreat when leader not in attendance

indicators.note: the leader, the first letter, is absent, so it is dropped

parts.note: to regress is to go back or retreat

explanation.surface: An army pulling back once its commander is absent.
explanation.definitionFit: An egress is an exit or a going out, so it names the act of departing.

clue.text: Perfume from city cruise on vacation

parts.note: Essen is a city in Germany

indicators.note: on vacation means emptied, leaving only the outer letters of the word

explanation.surface: A perfume bought on a holiday cruise from a city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on vacation' looks like a holiday but means the cruise is emptied to CE.
explanation.definitionFit: An essence is a concentrated extract used as a scent, so it is a fragrance.

clue.text: Bird left beneath the Rock with tail twisted

indicators.note: in a down clue the letter goes beneath, placed after the rest
the tail of the word, its last two letters, is twisted so they swap places

parts.note: Saint Peter was called the rock on which Christ would build his church

explanation.surface: A seabird perched with a twisted tail beneath the Rock of Gibraltar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Rock' suggests Gibraltar but means Saint Peter; 'with tail twisted' turns PETER to PETRE.
explanation.definitionFit: A petrel is a seabird that flies far over the open ocean.

clue.text: Problems returning section of Borg game

indicators.note: returning says the hidden letters are read backwards
section of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Trouble in a tennis match as Bjorn Borg returns serve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' sounds like tennis, apt for Borg, but reverses ORGGA. AGGRO is British slang for trouble or hassle.
explanation.definitionFit: Aggro is informal British for aggravation: trouble, hassle or aggressive behaviour.

clue.text: Country chatter extremely overblown

parts.note: gab means chatter

indicators.note: extremely means take the extreme letters, first and last, of the word

explanation.surface: Talk of a country that is wildly overblown.
explanation.definitionFit: Gabon is a nation on the west coast of central Africa.

clue.text: Tale about mother in dress of Hindu ex- resident at 12

indicators.note: the tale goes round the rest of the letters

parts.note: a lie is a tall tale

indicators.note: mother sits inside the dress

parts.note: a sari is the dress worn by Hindu women
ma is a familiar word for mother

explanation.surface: A story about a mother in an Indian sari who once lived somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: '12' points to the answer at 12 across, Elvis Presley's Memphis home; 'ex-' marks a former resident.
explanation.definitionFit: Lisa Marie Presley, Elvis's daughter, grew up at Graceland, his Memphis mansion, and later left it.

clue.text: Same-sex partner, one from British Isles

parts.note: a he-bride is a bride who is a man, the partner in a same-sex wedding
an means one, the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A gay couple from Britain, one of them introduced.
explanation.walkthrough: The Hebrides are island groups off Scotland's west coast; the same-sex partner is a groom-like bride who is a he.
explanation.definitionFit: Hebridean means coming from the Hebrides, Scottish island groups that form part of the British Isles.

clue.text: Live in revolutionary Iran after end of 22

indicators.note: the scrambled country comes after that single letter
end of takes the last letter of the answer to 22 across
revolutionary means the letters of Iran are turned about into a new order

explanation.surface: Living in Iran after a revolution, at the end of trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: '22' is AGGRO, whose end gives O; 'revolutionary' makes NAIR from IRAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A broadcast that is on air is going out live, as it happens.

clue.text: Actor fitted with new tooth

indicators.note: the actor's name is fitted with the extra letter inside it

parts.note: Michael Caine is a famous English actor

explanation.surface: An actor getting a new dental crown.
explanation.definitionFit: A canine is one of the pointed teeth between the incisors and the molars.

clue.text: Lauded one perhaps put on this cycle around estate

definitions.text: Lauded one perhaps put on this

indicators.note: the cycle word goes around the estate abbreviation

parts.note: to pedal is to cycle
EST is a common abbreviation for estate

explanation.surface: A cyclist circling an estate in praise of someone.
explanation.definitionFit: We put admired people on a pedestal, an idiom for idolising them, so it is where the praised are placed.
